outcome: No resolution of the Bass-Quillen conjecture in general has appeared since 26 January 2024, and the sources read (latest dated April to October 2026) do not describe it as solved; the in-window items are a torsor-level generalisation (Guo and Liu, preprint 13 March 2025, IMRN 6 June 2025), a single-version preprint (Stavrova, 21 December 2025) whose projective-module content for GL_r is the old dimension-two case, and a 2024 journal item (Chakraborty and Sharma) whose bearing I could not establish.
problem_asks: Let A be a regular Noetherian ring. (a) For every n >= 1, every finitely generated projective module P over the polynomial ring A[t1,...,tn] is extended from A, i.e. P is isomorphic to A[t1,...,tn] tensor_A (P/(t1,...,tn)P); equivalently every vector bundle over A[t1,...,tn] descends to A. (b) The Wikipedia lead, as frozen, states the consequence as a bijection between isomorphism classes of vector bundles over A and over A[t1,...,tn] (for each rank). Note from my own reasoning, not a source claim: the map from A-bundles to A[t]-bundles is automatically injective, since restricting to t=0 recovers P from P[t], so the substantive content of (b) is the surjectivity in (a). Scope words in the statement: 'every regular Noetherian ring' (no restriction on dimension, characteristic, or locality; the sources note Quillen's local-global principle reduces the problem to regular local rings) and 'every n' and every rank.

events.what_happened: M. P. Murthy, 'Projective A[X]-modules', J. London Math. Soc. (1966), cited by Stavrova as [Mur66] for the one-variable case of the conjecture for regular rings of dimension at most 2 (the Murthy-Horrocks theorem in the survey's wording). The general-n dimension-two case is credited to Murthy in the survey and in Stavrova's abstract, but I found no date for that general statement. The Murthy paper itself was not opened; the attribution comes from the opened Stavrova HTML and the opened survey.
events.delivers: For A regular of dimension at most 2 and n = 1: every finitely generated projective A[X]-module is extended from A (one variable only).
events.remains: Dimension at least 3 for n = 1 (except as in Rao's results below); all n >= 2 for dimension 2 is attributed to Murthy without a date in the sources; all n for dimension at least 3.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the proof in J. London Math. Soc. (refereed journal; the proof was not checked by me)

events.direction: Affirmative for the n = 1, dimension at most 2 case.

events.what_happened: Quillen (Invent. Math. 36 (1976), 167-171) and, independently, Suslin (1976): every finitely generated projective module over a polynomial ring k[t1,...,tn] over a field k is free. The Wikipedia article (opened) credits Quillen and Suslin and lists Quillen 1976 in Inventiones. The page numbers come from a search snippet of an AMS note; the Springer page for Quillen's paper returned a login redirect and was not read. Suslin's 1976 paper was not opened.
events.delivers: A a field: every finitely generated projective k[t1,...,tn]-module is free, for all n (the field case of the conjecture, which Serre had asked about).
events.remains: Every regular Noetherian ring that is not a field, which is the whole conjecture.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published independent proofs in 1976 (Quillen in Inventiones Mathematicae; Suslin venue not verified)

events.what_happened: H. Lindel, 'On the Bass-Quillen conjecture concerning projective modules over polynomial rings', Invent. Math. 65 (1981), 319-323 (volume and pages from a Stacks Project bibliography snippet; DOI 10.1007/BF01389017). The Wikipedia article (opened) says Lindel showed the conjecture for A a smooth algebra over a field. The survey (opened) and Popescu's 1989 work, as cited there, phrase it as regular rings essentially of finite type over a field. The Warwick lecture notes by Marlowe returned an unreadable PDF and were not read. Lindel's paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Affirmative for regular rings essentially of finite type over a field (survey and Popescu's phrasing) or for smooth algebras over a field (Wikipedia's phrasing). The two hypothesis sets are not reconciled here.
events.remains: Regular rings not essentially of finite type over a field: mixed-characteristic rings, and any regular ring not of that form; all dimensions and n beyond what the field-type hypothesis covers.
events.doubts: The sources phrase the hypothesis differently ('smooth algebra over a field' versus 'regular ring essentially of finite type over a field'). I did not read the paper to settle which is right.

events.what_happened: Ravi A. Rao, 'The Bass-Quillen conjecture in dimension three but characteristic not 2, 3 via a question of A. Suslin', Invent. Math. 93(3) (1988), 609-618, DOI 10.1007/BF01410201. The IAS repository record (opened) gives the title, journal and pages but no abstract. The survey (opened) lists the result as 'dim <= 3, d = 1, with 6 invertible: Rao'. The paper's text was not read.
events.delivers: Per the survey: the one-variable case (d = 1) for regular rings of dimension at most 3 with 6 invertible. The title indicates the dimension-three conjecture in characteristic not 2 or 3, via a question of Suslin. I did not verify the range of n covered.
events.remains: Dimension at least 4; in dimension 3, n >= 2 unless the paper covers it (not verified); characteristic 2 or 3 in dimension 3 per the title.
events.doubts: The characteristic hypotheses differ between the title (characteristic not 2 or 3) and the survey's summary (6 invertible). Both are recorded as the sources state them.
events.direction: Affirmative, partial (dimension three, with characteristic restrictions).

events.what_happened: Dorin Popescu, 1989 paper (title and venue not retrieved), cited in the survey and in Guo and Liu as the source, with Quillen, Suslin and Lindel, of the unramified case; search snippets attribute to it the extension of Lindel's theorem to every regular local ring containing a field, and the case of regular Noetherian rings in which every prime integer t is a unit or R/tR is regular. The 1989 paper itself was not opened. The survey (opened) credits Popescu with the approximation theorem used in the unramified case, and says the 'Henselian excellent case' claim from Popescu's 1989 results is 'incorrectly claimed' in a 2017 source.

events.remains: Ramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic, which the survey calls the main open case of the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Ravi A. Rao, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 325(1) (1991), 'On completing unimodular polynomial vectors of length three'. The AMS page returned HTTP 403 and was not read; the statement below is from a search snippet. Per the snippet: for a local ring of dimension three with 1/2 in the ring, a polynomial unimodular three-vector over R[X] can be completed to an invertible matrix; and if 1/3! is in R, every stably free projective R[X1,...,Xn]-module is free.
events.delivers: Snippet only: dimension three with 1/2 in the ring, for unimodular rows of length three over R[X], and freeness of stably free modules over R[X1,...,Xn] when 1/3! is in R.
events.remains: Projective modules that are not stably free; dimension at least 4; the characteristic conditions where not covered.

The abstract (opened, partially) states that a regular local ring is a filtered inductive limit of regular local rings essentially of finite type over Z, and that cohomological purity reduces to the complete case. The abstract does not mention the Bass-Quillen conjecture. Search snippets say the paper derives a Bass-Quillen consequence from a further question; the PDF was not read.

events.what_happened: Kestutis Cesnavicius, arXiv:2204.08233, first posted 18 April 2022 (v1 title, per a search snippet: 'The Bass-Quillen phenomenon for reductive group torsors'; the current title is 'Torsors on the complement of a smooth divisor'). The v6 abstract (opened, summarised by the fetch tool) completes the Nisnevich conjecture in equal characteristic and states as a byproduct 'a new proof for the Bass-Quillen conjecture for reductive group torsors over affine space' in equal characteristic. Mixed characteristic over a discrete valuation ring is covered under a quasi-split or Kisin-Pappas-type condition. The v6 comment says 'final version, appeared in Cambridge Journal of Mathematics; added several footnotes that correct inaccuracies in the published version'.
events.revisions: v1 18 Apr 2022; v2 29 Apr 2022; v3 16 Sep 2022; v4 7 Nov 2022; v5 14 Oct 2024; v6 6 Dec 2025 (comment: final version, appeared in Cambridge J. Math.; footnotes correct inaccuracies in the published version; 'added after publication' footnote on Theorem 6.1).
events.delivers: (a) Equal characteristic: for smooth X over a field, a smooth divisor D, and a reductive X-group G whose base change to D is totally isotropic, generically trivial G-torsors on X minus D trivialise Zariski-semilocally on X. (b) Byproduct: the Bass-Quillen statement for reductive-group torsors over affine space A^d_R, R regular containing a field. (c) Mixed characteristic over a DVR under a quasi-split or Kisin-Pappas-type hypothesis. Scope: torsors under reductive groups, equal characteristic for the main statement.
events.remains: The vector-bundle statement in mixed characteristic beyond the DVR cases; non-totally-isotropic groups (where Balwe-Sawant and Fedorov show failure of the torsor statement); the general regular Noetherian base. For G = GL_n, if it meets the hypothesis, the byproduct is the equal-characteristic vector-bundle case, which the survey attributes to Popescu and Lindel; I did not verify the GL_n hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Ning Guo and Fei Liu, 'The Bass-Quillen conjecture for torsors over valuation rings', arXiv:2503.10163 (v1 13 March 2025; v2 8 May 2025, 'to appear in IMRN'), published International Mathematics Research Notices 2025 (11), article rnaf142, online 6 June 2025 (per the OUP page). The abstract (opened) states: for a valuation ring V, a smooth V-algebra A, and a reductive V-group scheme G with a natural isotropy condition, every Nisnevich G-torsor on the affine space over A descends to a G-torsor on A (the main theorem sentence, 'every Nisnevich G-torsor on A^N_A descends to a G-torsor on A'). It generalises Raghunathan's theorem to a relative setting and extends Asok-Hoyois-Wendt affine representability to mixed characteristic. The introduction (opened in part) says the vector-bundle conjecture was resolved affirmatively in the unramified case or when A is regular over a Dedekind ring, citing Quillen, Lindel and Popescu, and that the mixed-characteristic torsor case was open before this paper.
events.revisions: v1 13 Mar 2025; v2 8 May 2025 (minor revision, 'to appear in IMRN'); journal version IMRN 2025(11), rnaf142, online 6 Jun 2025.
events.delivers: Torsor version: for A smooth over a valuation ring V and G reductive over V with an isotropy condition, every Nisnevich G-torsor on A^N_A descends to a G-torsor on A (mixed characteristic allowed). Scope: torsors under reductive groups over smooth algebras over valuation rings; the base is not a general regular Noetherian ring; not finitely generated projective modules as such. Recovers the vector-bundle descent in the valuation-ring-smooth setting where G = GL_n meets the hypothesis (not checked).
events.remains: The vector-bundle statement for arbitrary regular Noetherian rings, including ramified mixed-characteristic regular local rings (the survey's main open case).

events.what_happened: Anastasia Stavrova, 'On the generalized Bass-Quillen conjecture in dimension 2', arXiv:2512.18868 (v1 only, 21 Dec 2025; math.AG, math.KT; no journal reference or comment). Theorem 1.2 (read from the HTML introduction): for a regular ring A of dimension at most 2 and a reductive A-group G whose derived group is split semisimple, restriction to x1 = ... = xn = 0 gives a bijection H^1_Zar(A[x1,...,xn], G) to H^1_Zar(A, G), for every n >= 1; equivalently every Zariski-locally trivial G-bundle over A[x1,...,xn] is extended from A. The paper states the conjecture for regular A of finite Krull dimension (Conjecture 1.1) and says the general group version is known for equicharacteristic regular rings of arbitrary dimension and strictly isotropic G (citing [St22, Cor 5.5]), and for ind-smooth algebras over a DVR (citing Guo-Liu, Thm 1.8). For G = GL_r (derived group SL_r, split), the theorem covers rank-r projective modules over dimension at most 2 regular rings; the paper credits the one-variable case to Murthy [Mur66] and the general-n GL case to Suslin and Quillen. The paper's contribution beyond that is non-GL split groups. The intro does not, in the text read, call the general projective-module conjecture open.
events.delivers: For regular A of dimension at most 2 and reductive G with split derived group: every Zariski-locally trivial G-bundle over A[x1,...,xn] (all n >= 1) is extended from A. Restricted to G = GL_r this is the known dimension-two projective-module case (Murthy; Suslin and Quillen per the paper's attribution), so for the projective-module question its new content is only for non-GL split groups in dimension at most 2.
events.remains: Finitely generated projective modules over regular A of dimension at least 3 for every n; the general torsor version outside dimension at most 2 and outside the strictly isotropic/equicharacteristic cases.
events.time_since_posted: about 10 months (21 Dec 2025 to 10 Oct 2026). No citing or verifying paper found in my searches; the arXiv listing shows no journal reference.
events.doubts: Single-version preprint with no journal reference and no public engagement found. I read the HTML introduction and Theorem 1.2 through a summarising fetch, not the full text; the proof was not checked.
events.direction: Affirmative for G-bundles in dimension at most 2 with split derived group; the GL_r special case is the known projective-module case; no object.

disputes.summary: Popescu's v1 (1 Oct 2018) abstract claimed a proof of the conjecture for every regular ring; v2 (3 Oct 2018) recast it as a question, with the comment that Lemma 4 of v1 is wrong. The 2025 survey treats the ramified mixed-characteristic case as open, which does not fit a complete proof.
Banerjee's v2 (13 Dec 2022) claimed the dimension-three case with 2 invertible; v3 (14 Dec 2022) withdrew the paper, with the comment 'The proof of 2.2 is not correct'.

Whether the 2022, 2025 and 2025-26 papers (Cesnavicius, Guo and Liu, Stavrova) count as progress on the conjecture is a scope question: each proves a generalisation to torsors under reductive groups, and the GL_n instances coincide with cases already known. Records differ on how far they go; not resolved here.

Lindel (1981) is stated as 'smooth algebra over a field' by Wikipedia and as 'regular ring essentially of finite type over a field' by Popescu's 1989 paper as cited in the survey. The hypotheses differ and are not reconciled.

summary: The conjecture was checked through the Wikipedia article (last revised 22 April 2026, which states the conjecture and its known cases but gives no status verdict), the 2022 survey by Cesnavicius (arXiv 2201.06424, v4 of 5 May 2025, which says the main open case is the ramified regular local ring of mixed characteristic), and the primary papers listed in events. No event since 26 January 2024 resolves the conjecture as stated. The in-window items are: Guo and Liu (preprint 13 March 2025, IMRN online 6 June 2025), which proves a descent statement for Nisnevich G-torsors over smooth algebras over valuation rings, a torsor and mixed-characteristic generalisation; Stavrova (preprint 21 December 2025, single version, no journal reference), which for regular A of dimension at most 2 and reductive G with split derived group shows every G-bundle over A[x1,...,xn] is extended from A; and Chakraborty and Sharma (JPAA 2024), whose bearing I could not establish because the abstract was not retrievable. For Stavrova, the GL_r case is the projective-module dimension-two result already credited to Murthy (one variable, 1966) and to Suslin and Quillen (general n), so the projective-module content in the paper is not new for dimension at most 2; its new content is non-GL split groups, and nothing is claimed in dimension 3 or above for projective modules. Cesnavicius's 2022 preprint (v6 December 2025, Cambridge Journal of Mathematics per the arXiv comment, journal page not confirmed) gives a byproduct Bass-Quillen statement for reductive torsors over affine space in equal characteristic, which for GL_n would be the already-known equal-characteristic vector-bundle case if GL_n meets the totally-isotropic hypothesis (I did not verify this). Close calls: (1) the Popescu 2018 claim (v1) was withdrawn within two days, so it is recorded as withdrawn, not as a resolution; (2) Banerjee's dimension-three claim (v2, 13 December 2022) was withdrawn the next day; (3) Popescu's 2018 'On a question of Swan' answers a structural question about regular local rings, and its Bass-Quillen bearing is only asserted in a snippet, not checked; (4) Guo and Liu's introduction says the vector-bundle conjecture is resolved in the unramified case or for A regular over a Dedekind ring, which I recorded as their statement, not checked. The pre-window history (Quillen-Suslin 1976 field case, Lindel 1981, Popescu 1989, Rao 1988 and 1991, Murthy 1966 for one variable in dimension at most 2) is recorded as events because the status of the conjecture is built from them. The Balwe-Sawant (2016), Fedorov (2021) and Asok-Hoyois-Wendt (2018) items are neighbouring torsor results, recorded as separate questions; none of them addresses vector bundles over regular rings. AI search: no source names an AI system in connection with the conjecture or any of its cases, and I found no AI claim on it. The AI-claims index (aimath.robertj1.com) and ProofAtlas list the conjecture; in the parts of the index I could read, no entry concerns it. The OpenAI Astra list (ten results, August 2026, secondary reconstruction) and the 'over 100 problems' claim (21 September 2026) contain no Bass-Quillen item in the sources I read; for the 100-plus claim no list exists to check. Acknowledgements of Stavrova (HTML fetch), Cesnavicius v6 and Guo-Liu name no AI system.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a non-null count: Stavrova (2025) and Guo and Liu (2025) each extend the Bass-Quillen statement to new classes of objects in a way the field treats as progress, and Cesnavicius's 2022 byproduct is a new proof in equal characteristic. A reader who counts any such generalisation as a case of the conjecture would record in-window partial progress, and a reader who counts the Stavrova result by its dimension-two range might treat dimension two as settled for all projective modules. Against this, every in-window item concerns torsors under reductive groups or unimodular rows, and the one projective-module instance (GL_r, dimension at most 2) was already known. On the literal projective-module statement, nothing moved in the window. Whether a torsor generalisation 'changes what a careful person would write in this entry' is the judging pass's call.
what_would_settle_it: (i) The full text of Stavrova 2512.18868: whether the introduction calls the projective-module conjecture open, whether the GL_r case is explicitly named as the known Murthy and Suslin-Quillen case, and its acknowledgements (not located by my fetch). (ii) The Cambridge Journal of Mathematics record for Cesnavicius's torsor paper, to fix the publication date and confirm the GL_n hypothesis. (iii) The text of Popescu 1810.00617 v2 onwards: what the question is and whether arXiv 1803.06956 gives a Bass-Quillen consequence. (iv) The abstract and content of Chakraborty and Sharma, JPAA 2024. (v) Any 2026 paper on the ramified mixed-characteristic regular local case, which is the survey's main open case; my searches found none. (vi) The full AI-claims index (aimath.robertj1.com, 833 records, of which I read about 57) and the ProofAtlas entry for the conjecture, to confirm no AI-attributed claim on it.
